title: Non-blocking finding from PR #275's review (frontend vitest flaky timeouts under parallel execution)
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #275 (backend-cftc-cot-data-followups-followups, a docs/task-board-only change unrelated to any frontend file), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges. While running the standard `vitest run --coverage` gate as a baseline for that review, two separate full runs each hit one flaky timeout failure in the default parallel (84-worker) execution mode -- run 1: `FollowUpReviewDialog.test.tsx > records a review and closes the dialog on success` and `AddPositionDialog.test.tsx > sends the trimmed notes as entry_notes when provided`; run 2: a different pair of tests in the same two files (`AddPositionDialog.test.tsx > omits entry_notes from the request entirely when left blank` and the same FollowUpReviewDialog test again) -- each failing with `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms`. Re-running the full suite serialized (`vitest run --coverage --no-file-parallelism`) passed clean twice in a row (825/825, 99.76%/99.31%/99.78%/99.82% statement/branch/function/line coverage), and running the two files in isolation under default parallelism also passed clean (18/18). This PR's own diff touches no frontend files at all, so the flake is pre-existing and unrelated to it. A closely related, already-investigated flake specifically on `FollowUpReviewDialog.test.tsx` alone is tracked on `frontend-trade-journal-followup-review-followups-followups` (still `planned`, from PR #249's review) as a suspected one-off environmental fluke, having survived 13 isolated + 3 full-suite reruns with zero reproductions at the time. This review's observation adds new evidence against that 'one-off fluke' theory: the same test failed again on a completely unrelated PR, a second file (`AddPositionDialog.test.tsx`) now exhibits the identical symptom (a userEvent-driven MUI dialog form-submission test hitting the default 5000ms timeout), and the failure disappears specifically when file-level parallelism is disabled -- suggesting resource contention under vitest's default per-file worker isolation (84 workers spawned for 84 test files in this environment) as a more likely root cause than pure chance, particularly for tests that drive `userEvent` interactions through a real MUI dialog (async, multi-step user interaction simulation) under CPU/scheduling pressure from many concurrent workers.

checklist.step: Investigate whether AddPositionDialog.test.tsx and FollowUpReviewDialog.test.tsx's user-interaction-driven tests are being starved by vitest's default one-worker-per-file parallelism (84 workers spawned in this environment) rather than by a genuine race in the component/test code -- e.g. via vitest's own worker-count/pool tuning (`pool: 'vmThreads'`/`isolate: false`/`poolOptions.threads.maxThreads`), a higher per-test timeout for interaction-heavy tests specifically, or confirming this is a devcontainer-resource-specific symptom that wouldn't reproduce in CI. Cross-reference and reconcile with frontend-trade-journal-followup-review-followups-followups's existing checklist item on the same FollowUpReviewDialog.test.tsx flake (still planned) rather than duplicating the investigation from scratch -- consider whether the two findings should be merged into one task once a root cause is confirmed.

decisions.decision: Root-caused the flaky timeouts to vitest's default `pool: 'forks'` spawning one forked process per test file (uncapped except by `os.availableParallelism() - 1`, which was 84 on the host that produced the '84 workers' observation this task was filed from) -- not a race in the component or test code. Reproduced 5/5 times on a 24-core devcontainer with the suite's unmodified default config (`Error: Test timed out in 5000ms` in `AddPositionDialog.test.tsx` and/or `FollowUpReviewDialog.test.tsx` every time), then 0/7 across repeated full-suite runs (both via `--maxWorkers=4` and, separately, the committed `test.maxWorkers: 4` config) after capping worker count in `frontend/vite.config.ts`. Rejected `pool: 'vmThreads'` (the environment-reuse-per-worker approach vitest's own performance guidance recommends for this exact symptom) because it broke MSW's fetch interception suite-wide (`ReferenceError: TransformStream is not defined` -- a `vm` context's globals lack the Web Streams API that `pool: 'forks'`/`'threads'` inherit from Node's own process/worker globals) and would need a larger MSW/setup rework to fix, which is out of proportion to a flaky-test task. Rejected a global testTimeout bump alone (the checklist's other suggested approach) because it treats a symptom (occasional CPU starvation) rather than the cause (too many concurrent OS processes for the actual host), and a cap that fixes the cause outright needs no such compensating timeout increase. This finding is the same root cause as frontend-trade-journal-followup-review-followups-followups's FollowUpReviewDialog.test.tsx checklist item (both are the same 5000ms-timeout-under-default-forks-parallelism symptom, on an overlapping file) -- resolved there too via a cross-reference decision rather than duplicating this one, per this task's own checklist instruction to reconcile rather than treat them as two separate flakes.
decisions.rationale: The two prior investigations (13+3 reruns with zero repro on frontend-trade-journal-followup-review-followups-followups; 2 flaky runs on PR #275's baseline that filed this task) both ran the flaky file(s) either in isolation or on hosts with low-enough availableParallelism()-1 that the default worker count stayed modest -- neither happened to hit the specific combination of a high nominal core count and enough concurrent worker processes to starve a real-timer-driven userEvent interaction past 5000ms, which is why it looked like a rare fluke rather than a reproducible-on-demand contention effect. Explicitly capping workers removes the dependency on host core count entirely, so the fix should hold regardless of which devcontainer/CI host size it runs on next.

comments.summary: Independently reproduced the whole investigation: `--maxWorkers=23` (mimicking the old uncapped default on this review's 24-core host) reproduces `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms` in AddPositionDialog.test.tsx; the committed `maxWorkers: 4` passes clean (825/825, 84 files) and stays clean even under `taskset -c 0,1` (2-core-restricted, 3/3 clean runs, just much slower wall-clock: ~147s vs ~57s) -- confirms the cap is a genuine bound independent of host core count, not merely a higher threshold that a future higher-core-count host could still exceed. Independently reproduced the `pool: 'vmThreads'` rejection too: `ReferenceError: TransformStream is not defined` from MSW's fetch interceptor, exactly as described.

Non-blocking: the decision record's evidence trail is internally inconsistent about post-fix rerun count -- this task's own `decisions` entry says '0/7 across repeated full-suite runs' while the `frontend/vite.config.ts` comment for the same investigation says '0/4'. Tracked as a followup rather than blocking, since it's a documentation/evidence-consistency nit, not a functional defect (also caught independently by a code-review pass run during this review).

Non-blocking: `maxWorkers: 4` may be more conservative than necessary. During this review, `--maxWorkers=8` passed cleanly across 8 runs on the same host that reproduces the flake at higher counts, while running the full suite in ~33s vs ~57s at maxWorkers=4 (~42% faster) -- no evidence in the decision record that intermediate values were tried before settling on 4. Tracked as a followup for a proper tuning pass rather than blocking this fix, since 4 is safe, just possibly leaving CI wall-clock time on the table.

Independently confirmed the cross-referenced closure on frontend-trade-journal-followup-review-followups-followups is sound: its diff only flips the matching FollowUpReviewDialog.test.tsx flake item to done and adds a decisions entry explaining the shared root cause; the task's other two checklist items (isoDateWeeksAgo duplication, test.describe.serial due-trade-seeding edge case) are untouched and are genuinely unrelated findings from a different PR (#249) review.
